title: Build a greeting sub-plan
idea: TOOL: assemble a small program that defines greet() and calls it; predict and arrange.

exercises.prompt: GOAL: a program that shows 'Welcome!' using a sub-plan named welcome. First, what does the DEFINITION line look like?
exercises.explanation: A def line is 'def welcome():' - the word def, the name, (), and a colon. The body goes indented below.

exercises.prompt: Tap tokens for the def line of a sub-plan named welcome.
exercises.explanation: def welcome(): - that's the definition line. Next you'd indent the print and then call it.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the body so welcome shows the text:

def welcome():
    ____("Welcome!")
welcome()
exercises.explanation: Inside the sub-plan, print("Welcome!") shows the text. The call welcome() makes it run.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the whole program: define welcome (it prints 'Welcome!'), then call it.
exercises.explanation: def line first, indented print inside, then the call welcome() at the bottom. Define, then run.
The call welcome() runs the body, printing 'Welcome!'. Define sets it up; the call does the work.

exercises.prompt: You remove the welcome() call but keep the def. Now what prints?
exercises.explanation: Defined but not called means the body never runs - no output. The call is what produces the result.

exercises.prompt: To show 'Welcome!' three times, you can keep one def and call welcome() three times.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Define once, call three times. Each call re-runs the print. No need to re-define it.

exercises.prompt: Which is a GOOD name for a sub-plan that prints a welcome message?
exercises.explanation: 'welcome' describes the job honestly. Vague names like x or thing hide what the sub-plan does.

exercises.prompt: Match each line of your program to its role.
exercises.explanation: Three roles: define, body, call. The body runs only when the call fires - define is not run.

exercises.prompt: You just wrote and ran your first real sub-plan! The two things you did were...
options: define it with def, then call it with welcome()
exercises.explanation: Define with def welcome(), then call welcome(). That pair - define and call - is the whole tool. Nice work!
